body: `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes empty `data`. Prisma doesn't inject `@updatedAt` into an update with no fields, so this is a no-op, or at best a wasted query. `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` never actually gets bumped. If a timestamp refresh is the goal, set `updatedAt: new Date()` explicitly. Also, this runs on every cache refresh for every selected calendar of the credential, including ones not in `selectedCalendars` (other event types and integrations under the same credential).

`data` is typed as `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput`, which is the single-record update type and includes relation fields. `updateMany` expects `SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`. Relation writes aren't valid here, so this should fail typecheck or at runtime. Use `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`.

This throws a plain `Error`. tRPC surfaces that as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500), and the message may be masked. Throw `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" | "FORBIDDEN" })` like the other handlers. Also, the ownership check only matches `userId: user.id`. The UI shows the action for any Google credential that has cache rows, including team-owned credentials, so deleting cache for those will always fail with this 500.

This always instantiates the real `CalendarCacheRepository` and bypasses the `calendar-cache` feature-flag gating that `CalendarCache.init` uses to pick the mock. That adds an extra `groupBy` query on every `connectedCalendars` call even when caching is disabled. When the flag is off it can also report stale cache rows as a current "Cache Status".

`connectedCalendars` is shared by the v1/v2 platform APIs via `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb`, but only this tRPC path gets `cacheUpdatedAt`. Because the UI component is also used by platform atoms, cache status will silently be missing there. Consider whether that's intended.

The locale is hardcoded to `"en-US"` in `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, so every non-English user sees a US-formatted timestamp inside an otherwise translated string. Use the user's locale from `useLocale()` (`i18n.language`).

The read-only cache status block is wrapped in a `DropdownMenuItem`, which makes it a focusable, selectable menu item. Clicking it closes the menu and does nothing, and it's announced as an actionable item to screen readers. Use a label or non-interactive element instead.

After a successful cache delete, this only calls the optional `onSuccess`. It doesn't invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` the way the disconnect mutation does. Any caller that omits `onSuccess` keeps showing the old "Last updated" status and the delete option after the cache is gone.

Behavior change: this branch (a calendar that failed to load) previously ignored `disableConnectionModification` and always allowed removal of a non-delegation credential. It now hides disconnect when `disableConnectionModification` is set, so users can't remove a broken credential from here. Confirm this is intended.

`UserWithCalendars` now requires `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on selected calendars, but nothing in this PR reads them. Callers that build this type with their own select (`apps/api/v1/pages/api/connected-calendars/_get.ts`, the api v2 calendars service) must now select these extra columns or fail typecheck. Drop these if they're unused.

`sed -i '' -E` is BSD/macOS-only syntax. On GNU sed (Linux), `''` is treated as the script and the command errors out, so the env file is never updated. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` also depends on the caller's cwd rather than the script location.
